title: Mathematics

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

The Department of Mathematics has two admission pathways: Early Entrance and Standard Entry. For either pathway, visit the Department website for instructions to declare the major.

• Early Entrance: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 3.8 grade for each course required for admission

• Standard Entry: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 2.0 grade for each course required for admission; minimum 3.20 cumulative GPA in courses required for admission

The Department of Mathematics does not accept post-baccalaureate applicants.

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

The Standard option is intended for students who are interested in a versatile degree in Mathematics. Although the requirements for the degree are more liberal than those of the other options, the department recommends choosing electives with the idea of gaining more knowledge in a specific area of mathematics, possibly in conjunction with a minor in a related area. Students can choose coursework in algebra, geometry, topology, combinatorics, analysis, number theory, optimization and probability.
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

56-64 credits

• Core (28-36 credits) 

• Complete one of the following: 

• MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 207, MATH 208

• MATH 134, MATH 135, MATH 136*

• MATH 200, MATH 224, MATH 300

• Electives (28 credits): Seven mathematics courses at the 300- or 400-level, including three at the 400-level, excluding MATH 300, MATH 398, MATH 399, MATH 497, MATH 498, MATH 499. No more than two courses numbered MATH 380 or MATH 480. MATH 420 cannot be applied toward the three required 400-level classes.

• Minimum 2.0 grade in all courses presented to satisfy major requirements. Minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA in all mathematics courses at the University, including course repeats

• Minimum 18 credits of graded mathematics courses numbered 300 or higher taken in residence through UW, Seattle.

*May receive advanced placement (AP) credit for MATH 124 (after completing MATH 134) and MATH 125 (after completing MATH 135).
